text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Conservative coalition's campaign platform includes vow to freeze public spending for a five-year period, with a view to further cuts in labour charges.
-- Socialist and communist parties call for a boost in consumers' buying power and shorter work hours to stimulate economy.
-- Survey shows French are less pessimistic than they were in September 1996.
-- French postal service La Poste reports loss of 614 million francs for 1996, compared with 1.15 billion loss in 1995, and expects to break even in 1997.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Head of Erap holding company, which holds state's majority stake in nickel mining firm Eramet, Remy Chardon, criticises Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud's management of New Caledonia nickel conflict.
-- Government still expects to privatise insurer GAN before the end of 1997.
-- Regional mutual bank CMB to create some 360 jobs using Robien law that reduces labour charges for firms that shorten work hours to protect employment.
L'AGEFI
-- French GDP rose 1.5 percent year-on-year in 1996, mandatory contributions rose to more than 45 percent of GDP, public deficit at 4.2 percent of GDP.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Stockmarket regulator COB asks listed companies to provide better financial information to investors, forbids denials of correct information disclosed by third parties.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Unemployment decreased by 0.2 percent in March.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Germany's political establishment rejects speech by President Roman Herzog that portrayed nation as slow to make social and economic changes.
-- Good news on U.S. inflation ignites Wall Street.
